dominant_strengths: Massive confident display type anchors the page with strong hierarchy and clean optical balance against the black canvas.
Showcase strip of customer sites at the fold provides immediate proof-of-product, doing double duty as gallery and credibility.
Restrained monochrome chrome lets colorful template thumbnails pop without competing for attention.
dominant_weaknesses: Layout is the now-default dark hero + giant headline + template grid template; little distinguishes it from Webflow, Vercel, Linear clones.
Subhead is long and gray-on-black, weakening readability and diluting the punch of the headline above it.
Cookie banner overlaps a showcase tile awkwardly, and 'State of Sites' eyebrow feels disconnected from the main message.
fix_priorities: Tighten subhead copy and raise contrast so the value prop reads in one glance.
Introduce a signature visual motif (motion, canvas interaction) to escape generic dark-hero territory.
Reposition cookie/consent UI so it never collides with showcase content.
Differentiate primary vs secondary CTA more clearly via color, not just fill weight.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral impact from scale and showcase is solid, behavioral nav is conventional and clear, but reflective distinctiveness is low because the pattern feels borrowed.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it credibly communicates Framer as a serious site builder via typography authority and live customer examples, though it under-expresses the tool's own creative DNA.
